blocks.content: Real applications rarely run as a single container, a typical app needs its own service, a database, and a cache, at minimum. Docker Compose lets you define that whole stack in one file and bring it all up with one command.
1. The Problem With Plain docker run
blocks.text: 1. The Problem With Plain docker run

blocks.content: Running a multi-container app by hand means several separate docker run commands, each with its own set of flags for ports, volumes, environment variables, and networks, that has to be typed (or scripted) correctly, in the right order, every single time.

blocks.alt: Several commands to remember, in the right order, every time

blocks.content: 2. One File Describes the Whole Stack
blocks.text: 2. One File Describes the Whole Stack

blocks.content: A docker-compose.yml file replaces all of that with a single, declarative description: every service, its image or build instructions, its ports, its environment, its volumes, and how it connects to the others, in one place.

blocks.alt: The whole stack, described in one readable file

blocks.content:
services:
  app:
    build: .
    ports: ["3000:3000"]
  db:
    image: postgres:15

code.content:
services:
  app:
    build: .
    ports: ["3000:3000"]
  db:
    image: postgres:15

codes.yaml:
services:
  app:
    build: .
    ports: ["3000:3000"]
  db:
    image: postgres:15

blocks.content: docker compose up reads that file and starts every service it describes, networked together correctly, in the right dependency order, replacing what would otherwise be several manually sequenced docker run commands.

blocks.alt: Every service, started and networked, in one command

blocks.content: 4. The Same Stack, for Every Teammate
blocks.text: 4. The Same Stack, for Every Teammate

blocks.content: Because the whole stack is defined in a single file that lives in the repository, any teammate gets an identical local environment just by running the same command, this is the direct extension of the "works on my machine" fix Docker itself provides, now applied to an entire multi-service stack.

blocks.alt: The exact same stack, for anyone who checks out the repo

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Docker Compose replaces a manual sequence of docker run commands with one declarative file and one command to bring the whole stack up.
Because that file lives in the repository, every teammate gets an identical, reproducible local multi-container environment.
